articles.title: Europe’s wildest pilgrimage route: a trek through the mountains of north-west Sweden
articles.summary: A remote 18th-century chapel deep in Sami lands is the goal of the Präststigen, a 37-mile trail that traverses some of the country’s most spectacular scenery. I wasn’t exactly in “Sunday best”, but I had made some effort.
body: I had hiked to Alkavare following the Präststigen, or “Priests’ trail”, a 37-mile (60km) route from Kvikkjokk that could stake a claim as Europe’s wildest pilgrimage route, and certainly one of its most beautiful. The Präststigen follows the path that priests would once have taken to the chapel, built in 1788, to perform a service each summer, and today, on the last weekend in July, intrepid hikers and perseverant pilgrims can attend that same service.

Alkavare sits on the western border of Sweden’s Sarek national park, home to many of the country’s highest mountains and steepest valleys, yet with no campsites or tourist huts and only scant sections of the more famous Kungsleden trail. There are no other marked paths and to hike here means wild camping, a heavy backpack and a sense of adventure. It was described by famed Swedish diplomat Dag Hammarskjöld in 1926 as vår sista stora vildmark – “ our last great wilderness”.

articles.title: A moment that changed me: I spent a day with some naturists – and it cured my shy bladder
articles.summary: For decades, I had been haunted by paruresis, an inability to urinate in public toilets. But that day of nakedness suddenly, surprisingly, led me to shed my inhibitions. For as long as I can remember, I’ve suffered from a condition called paruresis – also known as shy bladder syndrome.
body: I’m a writer, so am often out and about meeting people in cafes, hotels and at events. My agricultural background means I also meet a lot of my interviewees on farms – but at least there I could pop behind a hedge if I needed to go, and be assured of privacy.

It was while I was doing research for a book on the spiritual connections humans once had with the land that I stumbled across the Christian Naturist Fellowship: a network of people who believe that Christianity and naturism are entirely compatible. Here, I thought, were a community who clearly get closer to nature than most – I was keen to meet them.

One of their committee members, Nigel, suggested I visit his naturist club near Colchester. So one Saturday morning in 2025, I set off to discover what Christian naturists really think and do. He had said that I’d not have to strip off – many don’t on their first visit – but when the time came, that is exactly what I did.

articles.title: I climbed into the car with three friends. I woke in hospital to find I’d lost them all – and my legs
articles.summary: Rob Pike was 17 when he and three of his closest friends were in a car that smashed into a tree and split in half. He explains how he coped with the devastation. After the car stopped rolling and came to rest on its side, Rob Pike remembers being “hyperfixated” on the rainwater pouring down his…
body: He was in the back seat next to his best friend, Daniel McCoy. “I look up to my left to see if Daniel’s OK. He’s probably about a foot away from my face and … he’s not OK. I’m looking at my dead best friend and I wish that wasn’t my last memory of him, seeing how broken he was.” They were 17.

“I lost control,” he says. “I am screaming at the top of my lungs. I’m yelling, I’m crying.” Even though he knew that Daniel was dead, he hoped for a miracle. “You spend your life watching Home and Away and Neighbours and you see people getting pulled out of cars and having CPR. If I can scream loud enough, then maybe somebody might come along and save his life.”

A woman had rushed out of her house when she heard the crash and run towards Pike’s screams. She found the car in the bushes. Pike remembers begging her: “‘Please help Daniel. You gotta do something.’ And then she gets down on her hands and knees, in the mud, in the rain, and she looks inside. And I remember her saying: ‘There’s nothing we can do for him. He’s already gone.’

articles.title: Babies born to anaemic mothers have smaller brains, study finds
articles.summary: Key regions of the brain linked to movement, learning and emotions were affected and may lead to cognitive problems. Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.
body: Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.

More than a third of pregnant women worldwide have anaemia – a condition typically caused by iron deficiency in which the number of red blood cells in the body is lower than normal. Symptoms include fatigue, shortness of breath and dizziness. Rates are highest in sub-Saharan Africa and south Asia.

Researchers from King’s College London in the UK, and the University of Cape Town in South Africa, followed more than 300 mothers and their babies in Cape Town, scanning the brains of the infants several times between the ages of three months and two years.

On average, the total brain volume of babies born to anaemic mothers was 4% lower than that of babies born to non-anaemic mothers – despite all the anaemic mothers being diagnosed only with a mild version of the condition.

articles.title: “Salomon Should Not Be a Fashion Brand”: The New Creative Director Shares His Manifesto
articles.summary: Despite substantial growth, the footwear brand is restrategizing. Creative director Heikki Salonen and CEO Guillaume Meyzenq want to unify Salomon’s hyper-technical product offering with the lifestyle-led designs.
body: Salomon sneakers weren’t always cool. Just ask creative director Heikki Salonen, who wants to restore the very geekiness that first attracted a trendier customer set to the French outdoors label. “When I started, I was adamant about the idea that Salomon should not be a fashion brand,” says the Finnish designer, video calling from Salomon HQ in Annecy, southeastern France. “We should keep on doing what we do the best, which is performance-driven — but performance in a non-traditional way.”

Salonen joined in January as the brand’s first official creative director, following a six-year stint as the anonymous creative director of Maison Margiela’s legacy diffusion line, MM6. Before that, he’d worked as collection director — leading on clothing — from around 2013. During his time at MM6, he oversaw several collaborations with Salomon, quickly recognizing a market for fashion-forward performance shoes.

articles.title: Meet Fashion’s Newest Engagement Metric: AI Visibility
articles.summary: As the models behind AI search increasingly surface earned media, PR is gaining new weight in the battle for brand discovery. Launchmetrics wants to prove, and measure, how brands win at AI search.
body: Brand perception is notoriously hard to measure, and AI is only complicating the equation. Few know this better than Rachna Shah, CEO of KCD, who says that over the past year, a growing number of larger fashion houses are approaching the agency expecting generative engine optimization (GEO) strategies — marketing practices designed to help brands surface within AI search results — to be baked into their PR plans.

“It first started coming up over a year ago, especially during new business proposals,” she says. “A lot of larger global strategic brands are asking us how we’re utilizing AI insights, looking at GEO and analyzing it — the appetite from brands is definitely there.” KCD has long worked with tech and social data analytics provider Launchmetrics to provide its clients with MIV (media impact value) rankings that track metrics like reach in search and how much social conversation brands are gaining. Shah says the brands that typically paid closer attention to these rankings are the ones that came knocking on KCD’s door first for AI visibility metrics.

articles.title: What Is Half-and-Half, Exactly?
articles.summary: You’ve probably been putting half-and-half in your coffee for years without knowing the full story.
body: Despite the promise of its name, the half-and-half you buy at the supermarket isn’t actually equal parts heavy cream and whole milk. While the dairy-aisle staple does fall somewhere between the two, and you can get away with substituting it for one part milk and one part cream in most cases, the truth is slightly more complex.

By law, half-and-half must contain between 10.5% and 18% milkfat. Most commercial products land on the lower end of that spectrum, at around 11.5%. The result is dairy that’s richer and more luscious than whole milk, but more fluid than heavy cream. Whole milk, meanwhile, has a fat content of about 3.25%, and cream contains at least 36%. Mix the two in equal measure, and you’ll end up with something considerably richer than most store-bought half-and-half. For a closer substitute, combine two parts milk to one part cream (~14%) or three parts milk to one part cream (~11%).

Your first interaction with half-and-half might have been those tiny cups that get tossed on the table at diners, fast food joints, and other less-than-fancy places. One or two of them does the trick to make even the cheapest, most burnt coffee taste better—or, at the very least, creamier.
points: You’ve probably been putting half-and-half in your coffee for years without knowing the full story.

articles.title: Which New York Shopper Are You — and Which One Is Your Customer?
articles.summary: In our ‘Neighborhood Watch’ series, we break down who is shopping where in global fashion cities. First up, NYC.
body: As brands look to invest in second, third, or even fourth, retail spaces in the cities where their best-performing stores are located, they’re having to get creative when it comes to choosing a location. It’s a careful formula, and one that relies on knowing your customer well.

Manhattan’s Madison Avenue and Meatpacking District may have been no-brainers for Hermès, but when the maison opened a temporary store in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, in 2022, some eyebrows were raised. Unlike the Upper East Side or SoHo, the neighborhood wasn’t traditionally home to luxury fashion brands. It soon proved the right bet: this month, the brand is opening a permanent space in the Brooklyn neighborhood.

articles.title: New York Fashion Week Cheat Sheet: Spring/Summer 2027
articles.summary: From DVF’s return to the fashion calendar to Thom Browne’s Tuesday finale, here’s what to expect and look forward to this season at NYFW.
body: Nothing says summer’s over quite like the post-Labor Day dive straight into New York Fashion Week. And this season’s schedule is jam-packed.

The official calendar commences tomorrow, September 10, with Henry Zankov’s anticipated debut as creative director of Diane von Furstenberg, marking the first time in nine years that the brand has appeared on-schedule during NYFW. But as usual, brands can’t help but get started early, with a number of off-calendar shows, store openings, parties and more filling the calendars of the fashion set.

On Wednesday, Rachel Comey, Cult Gaia, Ralph Lauren and Coach will host their runway shows, while the seasonal kickoff party of the week’s organizer, Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA), will take place at Rockefeller Center. Other parties from the likes of ShopMy and Bergdorf Goodman are set to go down, too, while Balenciaga is hosting an event at its SoHo store in honor of its new Hourglass Avenue handbag. Coach will be celebrating its 85th anniversary with a party right after its show at Pier 36.
points: From DVF’s return to the fashion calendar to Thom Browne’s Tuesday finale, here’s what to expect and look forward to this season at NYFW.
